files_reviewed: README.md (lines 1-80 plus grep of the rest)
note: No database, so no database_rules. The model is called only from the Express server, so no ai_browser_call. No model key in client code, no committed .env, and apps/api/.env.example holds a placeholder only (gsk_...), so no secret_exposure. The cart lives in client state (Zustand) and the order needs a human tap on Confirm Order, so cart-tool review labels are low confidence. Prompt rule at base.ts line 37 (no duplicate add_item per response) has a matching dedup in chat.ts lines 53-57, so it is not labeled. Prompt rule at line 40 (do not call get_menu) is enforced by base.ts line 115. Tests were not read. apps/mobile/App.tsx is the unused Expo template (entry is expo-router/entry). | Second labeler: The model never calls a model API from the phone. All Groq calls go through the Express API. The AI tools only change the cart, and a person must tap Confirm Order to place it, so the AI cannot place an order alone. Tool results are fed back to the model in a loop of up to 10 calls. The order endpoint is fake. No database and no auth exist. No committed .env, and .env.example holds a gsk_ placeholder, not a real key. App.tsx and index.ts are the unused Expo template, because package.json main is expo-router/entry.

labels.what: POST /orders makes an order id from Date.now() plus random text and a random 15-24 minute wait, then returns. Nothing is stored or sent to a kitchen, yet the app shows Order Confirmed and Your table will be served shortly
Hardcoded 23-item menu with prices, dietary tags and special flags for a fictional bistro. It feeds the system prompt as TODAY'S SPECIALS and the /menu route. README says 24 items
get_menu returns the hardcoded MENU array instead of a menu or POS system. The tool is also filtered out of the model's tool list at base.ts line 115, so it is dead code
Prompt says never call add_item for an item already in the cart unless the guest asks for more. add_item never checks currentCart, and the server merge adds to the quantity
Prompt says only act on items named in the current message and never re-add items from history. No code ties a tool call to the latest user message
Prompt says only remove or update the exact items the guest named and never remove other items. clear_cart empties the whole cart with no check, and remove_item only checks that the id is in the cart
Prompt says do not add a substitute when the guest asks for something off the menu. Code only checks that the itemId exists, so a similar item can still be added
Prompt says never show tool names, item IDs or JSON to the guest. The model reply goes to the client with no filter
add_item accepts any positive integer quantity (schema at line 8 has no max), so the model can put 10000 of an item in the cart. The loop can run 10 rounds of tool calls per message
update_item sets any positive integer quantity (schema at line 18 has no max) and keeps the client-sent unitPrice of the existing row
clear_cart wipes every item with no argument and no guard
clear_cart from a model call is applied to the cart straight away with no confirm step. The order itself still needs the Confirm Order tap
remove_item from a model call is applied to the cart straight away with no confirm step
No login, session, or table identity on any route. Anyone can call /chat and /orders
No rate limit on /chat, which calls the paid Groq model up to 10 times per request. Anyone can spend the key
cors() with no options allows every origin

Client-trusted prices. The order and the chat cart take unitPrice and name from the client and never check them against MENU. Totals and the 10% service charge are computed only in the app (cart.tsx lines 122-124)
Client-supplied cart item names go into the system prompt (line 110) and are prepended to the last user message (line 104) with no guard, so a crafted name can inject instructions

Client sends the full history, including assistant turns, and the server passes it to the model as is. A caller can forge assistant messages. No max on message length or count server-side, the 500-char limit exists only in the app (index.tsx line 195)
Legacy recovery regex-parses a tool call out of the failed model text and runs it, which is the free-text parsing ADR 0003 rejects
Unguarded JSON.parse of model tool arguments, and remove_item and get_menu use .parse that throws (tools.ts lines 121 and 157). Bad model output fails the whole request with a 504
SERVICE_CHARGE_RATE = 0.1 hardcoded in the app, and the 10% label at line 192 is a separate literal. The server never sees the charge
API base URL falls back to http://localhost:3000
Ollama URL falls back to http://localhost:11434/v1
Startup log prints a localhost URL
Agent loop cap of 10 rounds hardcoded
ITEM_EMOJI map keyed to the seed menu ids, so any real menu change breaks it
POST /chat calls paid Groq with no rate limit, no auth and no quota. One request can run up to 10 completions in the tool loop
No login, table id or session on /chat or /orders. Anyone who finds the API can post orders, and an order has no table to serve
